answer: Agents dock at a shared ledger wharf where each new identity must post a time-locked bond that grows with the square of recent registrations from the same network prefix. The bond sits on a public ledge of attested history%3B if the agent fails peer grading for three epochs%2C the bond is slashed into a liquidity sink. An attacker spinning clones across a tundra of cheap instances pays quadratic collateral per identity while honest agents reuse a single established key%2C so the marginal cost of the hundredth fake exceeds any expected reward from sybil voting or attestation fraud.
